title: When the Compass Wakes
premise: Wren Fairweather, a railroad engineer drowning in debt, inherits a dying prospector's map to the source of the Sable River — a place the railway company has bought up, fenced off, and forbidden. The map shows an abandoned spur line and something beneath the mountains that the company's ruthless director, Ambrose Vell, will kill to keep buried: a natural spring system that could make or break the entire rail empire. Pursued by Vell's enforcers and joined by a runaway telegraph operator named Isla and a disgraced river pilot called Marn, Wren follows the closed lines upstream, discovering that his own father helped build the fence around the truth. At the source, Wren must choose between selling the spring's location to clear his debt and destroying the company's claim by opening the waters to everyone — and he chooses to blow the dam of silence, flooding the records, freeing the river, and finding in Isla and Marn the family he never had.
about_author: Odile Sterling is a former surveyor's assistant who spent six years mapping waterways across the northern territories before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who follow rivers into trouble and come out changed.

chapters.title: The Weight of Brass
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Deep in debt to the Meridian Rail Company, Wren works the night shift repairing closed line signals when a bleeding prospector stumbles onto the tracks. With his last breath, the man presses a oilskin-wrapped map into Wren's hands and makes him promise to carry it upstream. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation born from guilt.

chapters.title: A Debt in Red Ink
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren examines the map at his boarding house and realizes it marks the forbidden headwaters of the Sable River. Company collectors arrive demanding payment; Wren learns Vell himself has posted a reward for a missing prospector's effects. Emotional beat: cornered desperation sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Girl on the Wire
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. Isla, a telegraph operator who intercepted orders about the dead prospector, tracks down Wren to warn him the company knows he has the map. She offers her skills in exchange for passage out of town. Emotional beat: two wary strangers recognizing shared enemies.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Using his engineer's knowledge, Wren and Isla slip out of the city aboard a maintenance handcar on a decommissioned spur. They evade the first patrol but find the track sabotaged ahead — someone else is heading for the source. Emotional beat: exhilarating escape shadowed by unseen pursuit.

chapters.title: Marn of the Shallows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Stranded where the rails end, they hire Marn, a river pilot barred from the trade after refusing to smuggle for Vell. Marn agrees to take them upstream as far as the Gorge of Bells. Emotional beat: grudging alliance forming the seed of a crew.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Marn's POV. On the water, Marn reveals the company drowned three valley towns to control the river's flow, and that her brother vanished investigating the source. Wren recognizes his own father's signature on the old condemnation documents she carries. Emotional beat: grief becoming common ground.

chapters.title: The Toll at Kestrel Bend
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. At a company toll station, Isla forges transit papers while Wren distracts the inspector — but Vell's chief enforcer, Corliss, arrives and nearly catches them. They escape downstream through rapids, losing supplies. Emotional beat: fear tempered by growing trust in each other.

chapters.title: Fathers and Fences
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A night camp conversation: Wren confesses his father built the fences sealing the headwaters, believing he was protecting the land. Marn challenges him — protection or complicity? Wren can't answer. Emotional beat: shame cracking open into resolve.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Bells
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The crew shoots the gorge's deafening narrows; the boat is wrecked, and they climb out soaked and half-starved — but the map survives, and Wren deciphers its key: the source lies behind a sealed tunnel on the old spur line. Emotional beat: survival forging unbreakable bonds.

chapters.title: Corliss Closes In
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. Vell's enforcer interrogates witnesses along the river, revealing Vell's true stake: the spring feeds every aquifer in the territory, and whoever controls it controls all settlement. Corliss burns a homestead for information. Emotional beat: cold menace raising the stakes.

chapters.title: The Town That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. The trio finds Bellhaven, a company-built town erased from maps, now inhabited by families displaced by the dams who survive outside the law. An old woman recognizes Wren's surname and spits at his feet. Emotional beat: belonging offered and complicated by inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Bargains in the Dark
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vell's agents reach Bellhaven offering amnesty to anyone who surrenders the map. A town vote nearly turns Wren over — until Marn vouches for him with her brother's letters, which name Wren's father as the man who tried to stop the drownings. Emotional beat: redemption glimpsed through another's faith.

chapters.title: The Old Spur
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Guided by a Bellhaven tracker, the crew reaches the sealed tunnel entrance on the abandoned spur. Wren repairs the ancient switch mechanism — engineering as inheritance, his father's craft used against his father's sin. Emotional beat: pride braided with sorrow.

chapters.title: Into the Mountain
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. Inside the tunnel they find the prospector's final camp and his journal: he was Vell's own surveyor, who discovered the spring could be opened to irrigate the whole valley — and was hunted for it. Distant explosions echo: Corliss is collapsing the tunnel behind them. Emotional beat: awe curdling into trapped urgency.

chapters.title: Time Running Out
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Racing through collapsing galleries, Marn is injured shielding Isla. Wren faces the map's final riddle — the source can only be reached by reopening a floodgate his father designed. He understands at last what his father left him to finish. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They emerge into a vast cavern where the Sable River is born, dammed and piped away to feed Vell's reservoirs alone. Corliss confronts them, offering Wren his debt cleared for the map. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. Corliss genuinely believes order requires the company's control of the water; he offers Wren not just money but belonging — a place in the machine. Wren looks at Marn bleeding and Isla waiting, and refuses. Corliss draws. Emotional beat: the corrupting logic of power stated plainly and rejected.

chapters.title: Let the Water Speak
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The climax: Wren fights Corliss on the catwalks over the cistern while Isla rewires the gate mechanism and Marn, wounded, holds the winch. Wren throws the lever his father built; the dam gates groan open and the river roars free down the old channels toward the valley towns. Emotional beat: cathartic release — the promise kept.

chapters.title: After the Flood
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. The released water swamps Vell's reservoir records exposed in the washhouse below; Corliss, choosing not to shoot, walks into the current rather than report failure. The trio escapes through the draining tunnels carrying the journal as evidence. Emotional beat: exhausted, trembling victory.

chapters.title: Vell's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Marn's POV. In Bellhaven, the journal and flooded aquifers spark open revolt; settlers seize the pump stations. Word comes that Vell has fled the territory, his empire of pipes worthless without the source. Marn lights a lantern for her brother at last. Emotional beat: justice arriving not as spectacle but as consequence.

chapters.title: Where the Lines End
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks later, Wren surveys the reopened valley for the settlers — paid in gratitude instead of wages, his debt dissolved by the town he once shamed him. His father's compass, recovered from the prospector's kit, finally points somewhere worth going. Emotional beat: quiet atonement.

chapters.title: Homecoming Water
chapters.summary: Ensemble close, Wren's POV. Spring comes to the valley; the river runs clean past rebuilt Bellhaven. Isla strings a new telegraph line, Marn launches a ferry, and Wren stands at the source with his found family, watching the water go where it will. Emotional beat: belonging earned, home made, story complete.
